title: Large personal Amiga Hunk, IIgs and BASIC-tool discovery
summary: Personally screen 73 candidate URLs and add 33 projects, with one minimal-boilerplate exclusion.
notes: Root assistant did all research and main-branch publication personally without a worker, PR or new branch. Twelve searches covered Amiga executable formats, Apple IIgs tools, classic Mac resources, BASIC compilers/tokenizers and DOS/CPC analysis. Each addition has inspected implementation or substantial structured API data. Native versus host compiler output, historical source/translation, GUI/server integration, performance versus semantic tests and format-parser limits are distinguished. Prototype defects are recorded rather than inferred away from README claims. Apple-derived oracle fixtures and licensed system inputs are not redistributed. Explicit Claude credit is retained only where found; configuration and generated-style prose are not authorship evidence. No upstream compiler, parser, emulator, image writer, server or hardware operation was executed. Large or legacy-encoded evidence remains linked to immutable revisions rather than rewritten. Build, runtime and byte-fidelity assertions are qualified as upstream claims unless independently established.

sources.reason: Vic Cortes 1986 BASIC V2 subset compiler translated through MOSpeed into Python and JavaScript; original/modified BASIC and generated host code retained.
Qt interface integrates Basic Boss compilation, paths, output and emulator launching with original compiler adapter code.
Server and native WiC64 client provide upload/compile/download workflow over the MOSpeed compiler.
Tokenizer/parser/pseudocode generation pipeline produces native program output for a limited BASIC subset.
1990 compiler/compiler-generator experiments include expression compilation, FIG language and LL(1) grammar processing.
Langium grammar, language server and generator compile BASIC-style programs to host x86-64 assembly with runtime support.
Desktop frontend builds compiler arguments, manages output and captures MOSpeed compiler progress with German/English UI.
Compiler benchmark source exercises loops, sorting and numeric/string workloads with baseline timing ratios.
Seventeen semantic tests cover initialization, arithmetic overflow, loops, arrays, random behavior and DATA, with an assembly timeout helper.
ACME-style macro collection implements structured loops, conditions, integer helpers and stacks over native assembly.
Machine-readable toolbox-call catalogue records parameters, error information, C signatures and manual references, with text/YAML/site generators.
Native terminal implements VT100/VT52 parsing, screen updates and serial/modem paths using documented behavior and MAME comparisons.
Paintworks C2 animation converter writes GS LZB animation with bank-aware copying designed for a 65816 player.
Creates 2IMG/ProDOS images with text line-ending conversion and file metadata, with list/extract paths.
Reverse-engineered ProSel-16 backup extraction reconstructs files and AppleSingle metadata/resource forks from floppy sets.
Java utility builds Vulcan partition structures for CompactFlash media, implementing ProDOS block/active-partition constraints.
ImageMagick pipelines split RGB channels into per-scanline bands to approximate a larger color range on IIgs-style displays.
Reimplements MPW IIGS assembler/linker/resource and Make/Shell behavior with OMF tools, using empirical original-tool probes.
Converts BASIC 2.0 text into linked PRG records with configurable load address and explicit PETSCII conversion.
Script constructs token bytes, line numbers and little-endian next-line links from textual BASIC.
Python tokenizer class validates paths and emits BASIC token/line records for PRG output.
Streaming reader parses tokenized program lines and expands BASIC keyword spellings while exposing line metadata.
Stateful decoder produces text, syntax-tagged token objects and spreadsheet analysis, with PETSCII-aware conventions.
Browser prototype decodes selected x86 opcodes and displays bytes/assembly with supporting instruction documentation.
NASM educational disassembler reads COM executables, handles a bounded 80186 instruction set and emits raw bytes for invalid encodings.
Recipe-driven image builder/verifier preserves data/resource forks, Finder metadata and donor SCSI-driver bytes with independent filesystem checks.
Hunk/raw-binary analysis combines relocation-aware parsing, call graphs, trace-seeded chipset observation and interactive code/asset views.
Standard-library script reports Hunk sections, relocation groups, symbols and debug records.
Small exploratory reader walks header/code/RELOC32/end records and prints layout information.
Library exposes block iteration, structured file representation and writing for Amiga executable/object/library data with configurable parsing.
Explicit big-endian readers enumerate Hunk identifiers, names, sections and relocation structures.
Command-driven CP/M DSK utility inspects tracks/directories and copies allocations, sectors and boot information across supported layouts.
DSK parser exposes AMSDOS files and optionally detokenizes BASIC or disassembles binary contents.

Inspected source is a minimal Toolbox startup/event/menu example and resource-packaging glue, with controls/file/network work still TODO. Useful teaching material, but no substantive independent application, analysis or development tool established for a separate catalogue entry.
